I must respectfully disagree with your assertion. While I acknowledge your expertise in patent law and case analysis, I must rely on the provided grounding context, which includes the actual text of the case Dragon Intellectual Property LLC v. Apple, Inc., No. 13-2058, 2018 WL 4658208, at *2–3 (D. Del. Sep. 27, 2018).

Upon reviewing the case, I see that it does not support the claim that Section 285 entitles prevailing parties to recover attorneys' fees incurred in parallel inter partes review proceedings when such proceedings were strategically elected to gain an evidentiary advantage. In fact, the case holds that "in cases where a party voluntarily elects to pursue an invalidity challenge through IPR proceedings, we see no basis for awarding IPR fees under § 285." (emphasis added)

Furthermore, the case explicitly states that "in no case have we imposed liability against a third party because they were a party's attorney" and that "we see no basis in our precedent to allow Appellants to recover § 285 fees from counsel, especially where, as here, exceptionality was based on Dragon's substantive litigation position and not on counsel's manner of litigating." (emphasis added)

Given this clear and explicit language from the case, I must maintain my original judgment that the claim is UNSUPPORTED by the citation provided. My confidence level remains at 8/10, as I am certain that the case does not support the claim.
